text:
carmen: quick heads-up — holdout sweep for rwd-embed-xlight on semantic dataset shows recall@5 regression after int4 quant.
ben: numbers? :eyes:
carmen: baseline (float32) recall@5 = 0.872
int8 (per-tensor) recall@5 = 0.848
int4 (naive) recall@5 = 0.781
also silhouette dropped 0.14 -> 0.09, clusters look smeared in UMAP.
cora: which holdout set and config? dataset name + seed pls.
carmen: holdout: holdout-2026-03-18 (wiki+qna mix, 50k queries). eval command:
```
python eval.py --model rwd-embed-xlight --quant int4 --holdout holdout-2026-03-18 --k 5 --normalize
```
run-bot: run 1765423460 finished in 4m12s — metrics uploaded to /tmp/evals/1765423460.json
ana: did you try per-channel int8 or asymmetric quant? naive int4 often shreds angular geometry.
evan: also check whether embeddings were L2-normalized before quant. cosine vs dot matters a lot.
mike: quick check — i re-ran int8 per-channel and got recall@5 = 0.859, silhouette 0.12. int4 with per-channel PQ-ish scheme bumped to 0.805.
carmen: thanks mike. can you push the per-channel run and config to the eval bucket? link?
mike: https://s3.redwood-inference/internal-evals/1765423501/config.json :thumbsup:
ben: would be helpful to see nearest-neighbor examples that flipped. any qualitative diffs?
cora: sample 42: float32 neighbors: [A, B, C, D, E] 
int4 neighbors: [A, X, Y, Z, E] — semantic mismatch at rank2-4.
ana: sounds like top-of-list degradation, maybe KV-cache prefix differences? but we're only embedding offline.
evan: also try using dot product on un-normalized vectors — some models are scale-sensitive after quant.
carmen: plan: 1) run per-channel int8 and int4 PTQ with outlier-clipping 2) run float16 baseline to confirm it's not FP32-specific 3) prepare 50 failing queries for eval set and cluster viz.
mike: i'll kick per-channel int4 with clipping now, will tag run as 1765423600.
run-bot: run 1765423600 queued on worker-7.
carmen: if int4 still bad we may ship int8-only profile for xlight and recommend quant fallback in optimizer.
ben: agree. also add a note in the model card about quant sensitivity and recommended eval prompts.
cora: i'll assemble the 50 failing queries and a quick UMAP snapshot. posting when ready.
ana: if we need immediate mitigation we can route prod traffic to xbase for Dedicated customers until fix. :shield:
mike: quick note — histogram of cosine shifts shows a -0.06 mean shift for int4, int8 is -0.015. attaching in thread later.
carmen: great, thanks team. tagging @ana @mike to follow up on remediation. :fire:
